stem.text: A wire is bent into the shape of the graph of \( f(x) = 2 x \sqrt{x + 1} \) for \( 3 \le x \le 5 \), with x and y measured in feet. Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression in terms of x that gives the length of the wire.

worked_solution.text: By the product rule, \( f'(x) = \frac{3 x + 2}{\sqrt{x + 1}} \).
The length is the integral of \( \sqrt{1 + \left(f'(x)\right)^{2}} \) over the interval: \( \int_{3}^{5} \sqrt{1 + \left(\frac{3 x + 2}{\sqrt{x + 1}}\right)^{2}}\,dx \).

options.label: \( \int_{3}^{5} \left(1 + \left(\frac{3 x + 2}{\sqrt{x + 1}}\right)^{2}\right)\,dx \)
options.derivation: the square root left off the arc length integrand

options.label: \( \int_{3}^{5} \sqrt{1 + \frac{3 x + 2}{\sqrt{x + 1}}}\,dx \)
options.derivation: the derivative left unsquared inside the radical

options.label: \( \int_{0}^{5} \sqrt{1 + \left(\frac{3 x + 2}{\sqrt{x + 1}}\right)^{2}}\,dx \)
options.derivation: the lower limit taken as 0, the start of the axis, instead of the left end of the stated interval
